polityNote: Republic of Latvia from independence (21 Aug 1991): 26 districts (rajoni) and 7 republican cities until 30 Jun 2009, then novadi and 9 republican cities. Atoms: geoBoundaries LVA ADM2 (State Land Service 2021, the parishes and towns of the 2021 reform; CC BY 4.0). Districts are unions of the parishes and towns their lv.wikipedia articles list for 2008, corrected by the parishes’ own histories (Nautrēni: Ludza → Rēzekne 1 Sep 1999; More: Cēsis → Rīga 1 Jun 2003; Lēdurga in Limbaži until 2009); novadi are unions of the parishes and towns listed for each in the 2021 en.wikipedia table. ① check — union areas against Statoids: the 26 districts on 31 Mar 2000 agree within −0.7%…−0.2% except Ventspils district −1.1%; of the 119 units of 2011, 110 agree within ±1.5% (Roja/Mērsrags compared as one), Olaine +3.7%, Ķekava −2.2%, Salaspils −3.9%, Saulkrasti −2.1%, Stopiņi −1.9%, and the cities Liepāja +13% (atom 68 km², stated 60) and Ventspils +5.5% (atom 58 km², stated 55 in 2011 and 46 in 2000: either a transfer from Ventspils district between 2000 and 2011 or a change of measure; lv.wikipedia gives the novads 2,472 km² = the 2000 district, so no transfer is drawn).

events.what: Nautrēni parish moves from Ludza to Rēzekne district

sources.title: Vikipēdija — Nautrēnu pagasts
sources.says: In 1998 Miglinieki parish was joined to Nautrēni parish; on 1 Sep 1999 Nautrēni parish was placed in Rēzekne district (before: Ludza district).

events.what: More parish moves from Cēsis to Rīga district (Sigulda novads)

sources.title: Vikipēdija — Mores pagasts
sources.says: In 2003 More parish was separated from Cēsis district and included in the newly formed Sigulda novads of Rīga district.

sources.title: Vikipēdija — Siguldas novads (2003—2021)
sources.says: Sigulda novads was formed on 1 Jun 2003 from Sigulda town, Sigulda parish and More parish; Allaži parish was added on 1 Jul 2009.

events.what: Districts abolished; novadi and 9 republican cities

sources.title: Vikipēdija — Latvijas rajoni
sources.says: Rajoni were units of the Latvian SSR and the Republic of Latvia until 2009; on 1 Jul 2009, with the territorial reform, the district councils lost their powers.

sources.title: Likumi.lv — Rajonu pašvaldību reorganizācijas likums
